meta.what: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) in Lean, Principia/Sha256.lean, run by Tests/Sha256.lean: NIST's CAVP response files for SHA-256, FIPS 180-4's examples, and the padding's size at each boundary of a block
meta.cavp_source: NIST, Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program, SHA test vectors for byte-oriented implementations: https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Algorithm-Validation-Program/documents/shs/shabytetestvectors.zip, downloaded 2026-10-15, 4909729 bytes, SHA-256 929ef80b7b3418aca026643f6f248815913b60e01741a44bba9e118067f4c9b8; its members shabytetestvectors/SHA256ShortMsg.rsp and shabytetestvectors/SHA256LongMsg.rsp copied byte for byte (CRLF line ends) to vectors/
meta.examples_source: FIPS 180-4's examples, as NIST publishes them beside the standard: https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Standards-and-Guidelines/documents/examples/SHA256.pdf ("abc" and the 448-bit two-block message; downloaded 2026-10-15, SHA-256 7006b6549dad2fc8c6f29417a921f2e48208157ef496a7e1e1d7d17c5cc1e7db), and FIPS 180-2, Appendix B.3 (one million "a"): https://csrc.nist.gov/files/pubs/fips/180-2/final/docs/fips180-2.pdf (downloaded 2026-10-15, SHA-256 1ac8c64a78c0b1e2fdb4c346da117fdf6bea713220a3b6d932080f1834d517c1)
meta.checked: before commit, every MD of the two response files (65 and 64 messages) and the three examples' digests were checked with Python 3's hashlib.sha256, an implementation independent of this one; all agree
meta.padding: a message of size bytes, each byte i % 251; padded is the padded message's size: the least multiple of 64 at least size + 9
